ev.amr_m_tonalli.text: The calendar priest leafed through his painted book for a long time and finally declared that your birth day was a good one; you would be named four days later, when the signs were better still.
ev.amr_m_comal.text: Before dawn {npc}, your mother, is patting out tortilla dough, and the same slapping sound comes from every courtyard in the ward. The first tortilla off the clay griddle is yours.
ev.amr_m_chinampa_mud.text: They gave you a small basket and set you to scooping mud from the canal bottom onto the chinampa bed. By evening you are covered in mud and the bed is a finger higher.
ev.amr_m_tlatelolco.text: For the first time you were taken to the market of Tlatelolco. Mountains of chillies, bundles of feathers, sacks of cacao, slaves in wooden collars, sellers shouting, and the market judges who see everything.
ev.amr_m_chili_smoke.text: The neighbour's boy was held over the smoke of burning chillies for lying. He coughed and howled for the whole ward to hear. You decided not to lie for a while.
ev.amr_m_telpochcalli.text: At the telpochcalli, the "house of youths", you sweep the yard, haul firewood for the temple and learn to hold a shield. At night there are songs and dances at the house of song.
ev.amr_m_calmecac.text: At the calmecac they wake you at midnight: cold water from the pond, prayers, then learning songs of the gods by heart and reading glyphs in the books. You are always sleepy.
ev.amr_m_cuicacalli.text: At sunset in the house of song young men and women dance to the huehuetl drum. The old women chaperones make sure nobody stands too close.
ev.amr_m_chocolate.text: At the feast you were handed foaming chocolate with vanilla and honey in a painted gourd cup. Bitter, sweet and spicy all at once. Commoners never drink this.
ev.amr_m_popocatepetl.text: Above the rim of the valley Popocatepetl, the "Smoking Mountain", gives off smoke, and beside it white Iztaccihuatl sleeps. The old people say they were once lovers.
ev.amr_m_algae.text: For dinner there are cakes of green lake algae dried in the sun, and fried little fish. Visitors wrinkle their noses, but you like it.
ev.amr_m_ballgame.text: On the ball court a heavy rubber ball bounced off a player's hip straight through the stone ring. The crowd scattered: by custom the winner may claim their cloaks.
ev.amr_m_canoe_dawn.text: For the first time you paddled a dugout across the lake by yourself. Mist, the cries of herons, fishermen with nets, and the white temples of the city rising out of the water.
ev.amr_m_texcoco_gardens.text: You were let in to see the ruler's gardens on the hill of Texcotzinco: water runs along stone channels into baths cut into the rock, surrounded by flowers from every corner of the empire.
ev.amr_m_poet.text: At the festival an old singer sang to the drum that nothing lasts forever on earth: even jade cracks, even gold breaks. Everyone fell silent.
ev.amr_m_octli_elders.text: At the festival only the old may drink their fill of octli. You watch grey-haired neighbours grow merry and loud while the young drink a single cup each and envy them.
ev.amr_m_turkey_dog.text: A turkey struts around the yard, as pompous as a judge, and a hairless itzcuintli dog runs underfoot. Your job is to make sure the turkey does not run off to the neighbours.
ev.amr_m_huehuetlatolli.text: An old man of the ward gave you the speech every young person hears: "The earth is slippery, child. We walk along a mountain ridge: a step to the left is an abyss, a step to the right is an abyss."
ev.amr_m_obsidian.text: You touched an obsidian blade in the workshop and your finger split open like ripe fruit. The craftsman laughed: "There is nothing sharper in the world."
ev.amr_m_tlacotli_family.text: A tlacotli here is not a thing forever: you have your own corner and your own mat, and everyone knows your children will be born free. That makes it easier, and more bitter.
ev.amr_m_rutuchikuy.text: Your hair was cut for the first time. Each relative snipped a lock and left a gift: wool, beans, a tiny llama figure. Now you have your real name.
ev.amr_m_chuno.text: At night the potatoes freeze on the hillside, and by day you trample them barefoot to squeeze the water out. In a few days they will be chuño, which keeps for years.
ev.amr_m_llama_spit.text: You were sent to herd llamas high on the puna. The wind cuts your cheeks, and the oldest llama, offended at who knows what, spat right in your face.
ev.amr_m_khipu_count.text: At the community gathering the khipu keeper ran his fingers over coloured cords and named how many people, llamas and sacks of maize the ayllu had. He never once got it wrong.
ev.amr_m_chasqui_pass.text: A chasqui runner sped past along the road, blowing a conch shell. At the relay hut his replacement was already waiting: he ran beside him for a few steps, heard the message and vanished round the bend.
ev.amr_m_terrace_song.text: The whole ayllu turned out to repair the terraces. The men set stones, the women carry earth, and everyone sings one long song. The work goes faster than you thought.
ev.amr_m_chicha_brew.text: The women chew maize and spit it into big jars: that is how festival chicha begins. A few days later the whole yard smells sour and sweet.
ev.amr_m_inti_raymi.text: On the shortest day of the year Cusco celebrates the Sun. On the square the Inca raises a gold cup of chicha towards the sunrise, and thousands of people fall silent.
ev.amr_m_royal_road.text: You walked the royal road: stone steps cut into the rock, a bridge of grass rope over a gorge, and on the hills rows of storehouses full of grain and clothing.
ev.amr_m_warachikuy.text: The initiation of noble youths: a race to the sacred hill, vigils, and at the end your earlobes were pierced for gold discs. Now you are a man.
ev.amr_m_cuy.text: Guinea pigs scurry across the kitchen floor, squeaking for grass. You have named every one of them, even though you know one will be roasted for the feast.
ev.amr_m_storehouse.text: The harvest was poor, but the curaca opened the storehouses and every family received its share of chuño and dried meat. Nobody in the ayllu went hungry.
ev.amr_m_apu.text: The snowy peak of Ausangate gleams above Cusco. Before a long journey you laid three coca leaves on a stone for the mountain spirit, the apu, so the road would go easily.
ev.amr_m_pichincha.text: The volcano Pichincha stands over Quito, its summit hidden in cloud each morning. It is always spring here: no winter, no summer, only rain and sun taking turns.
ev.amr_m_mitmaq_neighbours.text: The new neighbours came from the far south on the Inca's orders. They speak a little differently, wear different caps and miss their own mountains. You teach their children the local games.
ev.amr_m_yana_home.text: At night you remember your home ayllu: smoke over the roofs, voices, your own fields. You were given into service years ago, and there is no road back.
ev.amr_m_coca_leaf.text: The curaca rewarded your good work with a handful of coca leaves. Commoners are not supposed to chew coca, so you saved the leaves as an offering to the spirits.
ev.amr_d_school_vow.title: Telpochcalli or calmecac
ev.amr_d_school_vow.text: Your family must decide where to dedicate you. The telpochcalli is the youths' house of your ward: work, war, songs. The calmecac is the temple school: fasts, vigils, books and the road to the priesthood. Commoners are rarely admitted, but it happens.
ev.amr_d_school_vow.telpochcalli: The telpochcalli, like everyone in the ward
ev.amr_d_school_vow.calmecac: Ask the priests to take you into the calmecac
ev.amr_d_school_vow.calmecac.success: The priests agreed. Cold nights, books and strict teachers await you.
ev.amr_d_school_vow.calmecac.failure: The priests refused: there is no room for commoners' children. The gifts were wasted.
ev.amr_d_calmecac_later.title: The end of schooling
ev.amr_d_calmecac_later.text: Your years in the calmecac are over. The high priest offers you a place at the temple, serving the gods for the rest of your days. You could also return to your ward, where those who can read glyphs are respected.
ev.amr_d_patolli.title: Patolli
ev.amr_d_patolli.text: A cross of squares is painted on a mat, and marked beans are thrown as dice. Players stake cloaks, beads, cacao, and some, they say, have staked themselves. They make room for you.
ev.amr_d_patolli.play.success: The beans fall your way. You walk off with other men's cloaks, and a wish to come back.
ev.amr_d_patolli.play.failure: You lose everything you brought and promise to win it back.
ev.amr_d_octli.title: One cup too many
ev.amr_d_octli.text: Friends from your ward have got hold of a jar of octli and invite you outside the town. Drunkenness is forbidden to the young: anyone caught can have his head shaved in public, and a repeat offender punished more harshly.
ev.amr_d_octli.drink.success: A merry night, and nobody found out.
ev.amr_d_octli.drink.failure: You were seen. In the morning the whole ward watched you being shaved.
ev.amr_d_sell_self.title: Selling yourself
ev.amr_d_sell_self.text: It is a hungry year and debts are growing. Here a person may sell themselves as a tlacotli: the buyer pays a price, you work for him, and someday you can buy yourself back. Many save their families this way.
ev.amr_d_sell_self.sell: Sell yourself and feed your family
ev.amr_d_sell_self.borrow: Ask the ward elders for help
ev.amr_d_sell_self.borrow.success: The calpulli elders gave you grain from the common stores.
ev.amr_d_sell_self.borrow.failure: The ward's stores are empty. There is nothing to give.
ev.amr_d_buy_freedom.title: The ransom
ev.amr_d_buy_freedom.text: All these years you have saved a little at a time, cloak by cloak. Your master says he will accept the ransom if you add a little more.
ev.amr_d_buy_freedom.stay: Stay: here at least you eat
ev.amr_d_market_judge.title: The market judges
ev.amr_d_market_judge.text: A trader sold you a sack of cacao, and half the beans turned out to be empty shells stuffed with earth. The market judges sit under their awning nearby.
ev.amr_d_market_judge.complain.success: The judges hear the case on the spot. The cheat is punished and you get your due.
ev.amr_d_market_judge.complain.failure: The trader swears he sold good beans, and there are no witnesses.
ev.amr_d_porter.title: A caravan to the hot lands
ev.amr_d_porter.text: Pochteca are gathering a caravan for the coast and need porters. The road is long and crosses hostile lands, but they pay well, and you could come back with feathers and cacao.
ev.amr_d_porter.go.success: You came back half a year later, thin and sunburnt, with a bundle of goods on your back.
ev.amr_d_porter.go.failure: The caravan was attacked in the mountains. You escaped, but came home empty-handed with a bad leg.
ev.amr_d_porter_later.title: An old acquaintance
ev.amr_d_porter_later.text: The pochteca you once went to the coast with has grown rich and is looking for a reliable person to manage his business at the market while he travels.
ev.amr_d_matchmaker.title: The matchmakers
ev.amr_d_matchmaker.text: Old women matchmakers have come to the house: the groom's family asks for your hand. Custom says to refuse twice and agree the third time, and a calendar priest will choose the wedding day.
ev.amr_d_matchmaker.refuse.success: Your family grumbled but gave in. You will wait a little longer.
ev.amr_d_matchmaker.refuse.failure: Your family would not hear of it. The wedding will happen anyway.
ev.amr_d_name_day.title: An unlucky day
ev.amr_d_name_day.text: The calendar priest frowned: your {g=npc_sex:son|daughter} {npc} was born under an evil sign. You can delay the naming until a better day, and for a gift the priest will find one.
ev.amr_d_name_day.wait: Pay and wait for a good day
ev.amr_d_coatequitl.title: Communal labour
ev.amr_d_coatequitl.text: The ward must send people to build a causeway and a temple. It is your turn, for many weeks. You can buy your way out with cloaks, if you have them.
ev.amr_d_mita_turn.title: Your mit'a turn
ev.amr_d_mita_turn.text: The curaca has announced that this year it is your turn for mit'a: building a road far to the north. Months away from home, but you are fed from state storehouses and the neighbours will work your field.
ev.amr_d_mita_turn.plead: Ask the curaca for a delay
ev.amr_d_mita_turn.plead.success: The curaca nodded: you can go next time.
ev.amr_d_mita_turn.plead.failure: The curaca grew angry and sent you to the hardest stretch.
ev.amr_d_mita_later.title: The road you built
ev.amr_d_mita_later.text: A governor travelled along the road you once built. He asked who had laid the steps there and had you found: he needs a foreman for the new builders.
ev.amr_d_aclla_choice.title: Chosen for the Sun
ev.amr_d_aclla_choice.text: An Inca official has come to the ayllu to choose the prettiest and most skilful girls for the house of the chosen. There they learn to weave the finest cumbi and brew chicha for the gods. Girls do not come home from there.
ev.amr_d_aclla_choice.go: Go to the house of the chosen
ev.amr_d_aclla_choice.hide.success: The official did not notice you. You stay home.
ev.amr_d_aclla_choice.hide.failure: The deception was discovered. Your family was punished and you were taken anyway.
ev.amr_d_aclla_later.title: The Inca's gift
ev.amr_d_aclla_later.text: The Inca rewards distinguished warriors and loyal curacas by giving them chosen women as wives. The mamakuna, the senior priestesses, say the choice has fallen on you. You could also stay and serve the Sun forever.
ev.amr_d_aclla_later.stay: Stay as a mamakuna at the temple
ev.amr_d_ayni.title: Ayni
ev.amr_d_ayni.text: A neighbour asks you to help dig his potatoes tomorrow, exactly when yours are ready. Ayni is mutual help: today you help him, tomorrow he helps you. But the potatoes will not wait.
ev.amr_d_huaca_drought.title: Drought
ev.amr_d_huaca_drought.text: There has been no rain for two months. The huaca priest says the mountain spirits are hungry and asks every family for an offering: a llama from some, chicha and coca from others.
ev.amr_d_khipu_error.title: A mistake in the knots
ev.amr_d_khipu_error.text: The khipu keeper has recorded one more worker in your household than you have, so now you owe an extra share of labour. Arguing with a khipu is like arguing with the Inca.
ev.amr_d_khipu_error.argue: Go to the curaca and argue
ev.amr_d_khipu_error.argue.success: The knots were retied. The khipu keeper grumbles, but the extra duty is gone.
ev.amr_d_khipu_error.argue.failure: The curaca had no time for you. All you gained was an enemy.
ev.amr_d_qollqa.title: At the storehouse
ev.amr_d_qollqa.text: You have been set to guard a row of storehouses on the hill. At night a widow you know comes: her children are starving, and she asks for a little bag of chuño. Theft from the Inca's storehouses is punished harshly.
ev.amr_d_qollqa.give.success: Nobody found out. The widow will pray for you all her life.
ev.amr_d_qollqa.give.failure: The shortfall was found. You were beaten and dismissed from your post.
ev.amr_d_sirvinakuy.title: Trial marriage
ev.amr_d_sirvinakuy.text: By the custom of the mountains a young couple may live together for a year or two before deciding whether to become husband and wife. Such a union is being offered to you.
ev.amr_d_sirvinakuy.try.success: You grew used to each other. A year later you held the wedding.
ev.amr_d_sirvinakuy.try.failure: It did not work out. You parted peacefully, and no one blames you.
ev.amr_d_curaca_water.title: A dispute over water
ev.amr_d_curaca_water.text: Two ayllus are quarrelling over a canal: the upper one turns the water onto its terraces and the lower one gets nothing. Both sides await your ruling, and both have brought gifts.
ev.amr_d_curaca_water.gifts: Rule for the more generous side
ev.amr_d_chicha_feast.title: A chicha feast
ev.amr_d_chicha_feast.text: At the sowing festival the curaca treats everyone to chicha from huge jars. Drinking here is a duty to the spirits, and refusing is rude. But by morning many cannot stand.
ev.amr_d_chicha_feast.polite: Drink a couple of cups to be polite
ev.amr_d_pichca.title: Pichca dice
ev.amr_d_pichca.text: By the fire people are playing pichca: throwing a five-sided bone die and moving beans across a board. The stakes are wool, chillies, even a llama.
ev.amr_d_pichca.play.success: You won two llamas and a sack of chillies!
ev.amr_d_pichca.play.failure: The llama went to a new owner. And your hands still itch for the die.
ev.amr_d_inca_wedding.title: The day of weddings
ev.amr_d_inca_wedding.text: Once a year an Inca official gathers the community's young people and announces the couples. You have been paired with someone you barely know. You could ask the curaca for a different match.
ev.amr_d_inca_wedding.ask.success: The curaca knows your family and gave way. The match will be one you want.
ev.amr_d_inca_wedding.ask.failure: The Inca's decisions are not changed.
ev.amr_d_sirvinakuy.note: Trial marriage (sirvinakuy, "serving each other") was described by Spanish writers in colonial times; it is thought to go back to before the Incas and survives in the Andes today.
ev.amr_d_inca_wedding.note: Chroniclers such as Garcilaso and Guaman Poma wrote that Inca officials held mass weddings in the communities every year. Historians argue over how compulsory this really was.
ev.amr_t_captured.title: Taken captive
ev.amr_t_captured.text: In a "flower war" with Tlaxcala you were surrounded and knocked down. Now you are a captive in an enemy city, and here, as at home, captives are kept for the festival of the gods.
ev.amr_t_captured.escape.success: You climbed the fence and walked three nights through the mountains. At home they greeted you as one returned from the dead.
ev.amr_t_captured.escape.failure: You were caught right at the border. No one saw you again.
ev.amr_t_captured.wait: Wait for an exchange of captives
ev.amr_t_captured.wait.success: The noble houses agreed on an exchange. You were released, alive and changed forever.
ev.amr_t_spy_merchant.title: A merchant in disguise
ev.amr_t_spy_merchant.text: The ruler has summoned you to the palace. He needs someone to go to the markets of a hostile city disguised as a local trader, learn the language, wear their clothes and remember where the forts stand.
ev.amr_t_spy_merchant.go.success: You came back with the news, and the ruler rewarded you generously with land and honours.
ev.amr_t_spy_merchant.go.failure: You were found out on the third day. You barely escaped, abandoning all your goods.
ev.amr_t_flood.title: The water has risen
ev.amr_t_flood.text: After long rains the lake has burst its banks. The chinampas are washed away and the mud walls of your house are sinking. Relatives in Texcoco invite you to come: the shore is higher there.
ev.amr_t_jade.title: The green stone
ev.amr_t_jade.text: Digging a hole for a new post, you came upon an old cache: beads of chalchihuitl jade and a small figure of a god. Here jade is worth more than gold.
ev.amr_t_jade.sell: Sell it secretly to a lord
ev.amr_t_jade.sell.success: The lord paid generously and asked no questions.
ev.amr_t_jade.sell.failure: The lord took the jade and threatened to report you if you talked.
ev.amr_t_jade.keep: Hide it for a rainy day
ev.amr_t_gambling_debt.title: Lost at patolli
ev.amr_t_gambling_debt.text: You have lost so much at patolli that you have nothing left to pay. The winner calmly says that by custom you will become his tlacotli until the debt is worked off.
ev.amr_t_gambling_debt.flee.success: You hid in Texcoco and started over.
ev.amr_t_gambling_debt.flee.failure: You were found and brought back, now in disgrace as well.
ev.amr_t_palace_call.title: Work for the palace
ev.amr_t_palace_call.text: The palace steward has seen your work. The ruler needs craftsmen at court: they are fed from the royal kitchens and given a house, but mistakes there are not forgiven.
ev.amr_t_palace_call.go.success: The ruler himself wears your work. You are now a person of standing.
ev.amr_t_palace_call.go.failure: The commission displeased them. You were thrown out in disgrace.
ev.amr_t_yana_taken.title: Taken as a yana
ev.amr_t_yana_taken.text: An Inca noble passing through the ayllu pointed at you: he needs servants. If you become a yana there is no road back to your community, but his house is rich and powerful.
ev.amr_t_yana_taken.curaca.success: The curaca said the community needed you for mit'a, and the noble backed down.
ev.amr_t_yana_taken.curaca.failure: The curaca did not dare argue with an Inca.
ev.amr_t_curaca_chosen.title: A new curaca
ev.amr_t_curaca_chosen.text: The old curaca has died without grown sons. The ayllu elders gathered and named you: you know every family and every stone on the terraces.
ev.amr_t_curaca_chosen.refuse: Refuse: it is not for you
ev.amr_t_earthquake.title: The earth shook
ev.amr_t_earthquake.text: At night the ground roared and heaved. Walls of rough stone collapsed and the roof buried the stores. Only the old Inca walls stand as if nothing had happened.
ev.amr_t_earthquake.dig: Dig through the rubble to save the stores
ev.amr_t_earthquake.dig.failure: Another wall collapsed. You were badly hurt.
ev.amr_t_inca_reward.title: The Inca's reward
ev.amr_t_inca_reward.text: After the victory the Inca hands out rewards to those who distinguished themselves. You are offered a choice: fine cumbi cloth and a herd of llamas, or an honourable post on the far frontier of the realm.
ev.amr_mv_mitmaq.title: Resettlement
ev.amr_mv_mitmaq.text: The Inca has decreed that part of your ayllu will go north to Quito to guard the new lands and teach the locals Inca ways. The curaca is drawing up the lists. Volunteers are promised the best fields.
ev.amr_mv_mitmaq.note: The Incas moved whole communities, the mitmaqkuna, from old provinces to new ones and back again, to secure conquests and break up rebellious peoples. Settlers from the south lived around Quito.
ev.amr_mv_hostage_son.title: Schooling in Cusco
ev.amr_mv_hostage_son.text: The sons of local curacas must live in Cusco to learn the Inca language, khipus and customs, and also to serve as a guarantee of their fathers' loyalty. Now it is your turn.
ev.amr_mv_hostage_son.delay.success: The departure was postponed. You stay home another year.
ev.amr_mv_hostage_son.delay.failure: The official did not believe you. You were sent off under guard.
ev.amr_mv_hostage_son.note: The Incas took the sons of conquered rulers to Cusco, where they were taught at the school for nobles (yachay wasi). This trained loyal local leaders and kept their fathers from rebelling.
ev.amr_mv_to_capital.title: To the great city
ev.amr_mv_to_capital.text: A canoeman you know says that in Tenochtitlan they build, trade and feast day and night, and there is always work for willing hands. The island is half a day away by dugout.
ev.amr_mv_texcoco_scholars.title: The city of sages
ev.amr_mv_texcoco_scholars.text: In Texcoco the ruler's court gathers singers, stargazers, lawmakers and the finest tlacuilos. They say pupils from any city of the Alliance are taken there.
ev.amr_mv_quito_return.title: Longing for the south
ev.amr_mv_quito_return.text: You dream more and more often of the mountains of Cusco. A tribute caravan is heading south, and the khipu keeper is willing to list you as a porter.
ev.amr_j_first_captive.title: Your first captive
ev.amr_j_first_captive.text: In battle you knocked an enemy warrior off his feet. If you can bring him back to camp alive, you will earn the right to a new hairstyle and your first embroidered cloak.
ev.amr_j_first_captive.take.success: You brought the captive in. The veteran warriors clap you on the shoulder.
ev.amr_j_first_captive.take.failure: The captive was snatched back and you were wounded.
ev.amr_j_first_captive.share: Call a comrade and share the glory
ev.amr_j_eagle.title: The order of Eagles
ev.amr_j_eagle.text: You have taken your fourth captive. The Eagle and Jaguar warriors invite you into their order: a place in their house at the palace, the right to wear feathers and sandals in the city, and the front line in every battle.
ev.amr_j_quetzal.title: Quetzal feathers
ev.amr_j_quetzal.text: The palace has ordered a quetzal-feather headdress for the festival. The feathers sent are barely enough, and one wrong move will ruin their shimmering green.
ev.amr_j_quetzal.careful.success: The headdress shines. They say the ruler himself smiled.
ev.amr_j_quetzal.careful.failure: You missed the deadline. The steward is displeased.
ev.amr_j_quetzal.parrot.success: No one noticed the swap, and you sold the feathers you saved.
ev.amr_j_quetzal.parrot.failure: The connoisseurs saw the swap at once. Disgrace before the whole artisans' quarter.
ev.amr_j_own_workshop.title: A workshop of your own
ev.amr_j_own_workshop.text: An old master in the featherworkers' quarter is going blind and offers you his workshop, with apprentices, a store of feathers and customers from the palace.
ev.amr_j_pochteca_return.title: Coming home by night
ev.amr_j_pochteca_return.text: The caravan has returned from Xicalanco with rich goods. The senior pochteca teach: enter the city at night, hide your wealth, walk in a plain cloak; the nobility does not like upstarts.
ev.amr_j_pochteca_return.feast: Throw a feast for the whole ward
ev.amr_j_pochteca_return.feast.success: The feast was a triumph and everyone praises you. For now the nobles look the other way.
ev.amr_j_pochteca_return.feast.failure: The nobles thought you an upstart. They will remember it.
ev.amr_j_pochteca_road.title: Ambush in the mountains
ev.amr_j_pochteca_road.text: On the road to the coast a scout reports that a hostile people is waiting for the caravan in a gorge. You could fight through, for pochteca know how to fight, or spend a week going round.
ev.amr_j_pochteca_road.fight.success: You broke through. The ruler will grant you insignia for your courage.
ev.amr_j_pochteca_road.fight.failure: You broke through, but at a cost: half the goods and porters were left in the gorge.
ev.amr_j_chinampa_new.title: A new bed
ev.amr_j_chinampa_new.text: At the edge of the ward there is a strip of shallow water. Drive in willow stakes, weave the walls, haul in mud, and in a year there will be a new chinampa. It is a whole season's work.
ev.amr_j_chinampa_rich.title: The new bed's harvest
ev.amr_j_chinampa_rich.text: The chinampa you once built with your own hands now feeds your whole family and gives a surplus for the market. Neighbours come asking for advice.
ev.amr_j_chinampa_rich.share: Help the neighbours build their own
ev.amr_j_canoe_storm.title: Wind on the lake
ev.amr_j_canoe_storm.text: A wind has come up in the middle of the lake, and waves are swamping your dugout, loaded with stone for a building site. The load is dragging it down.
ev.amr_j_canoe_storm.push: Paddle for shore with the load
ev.amr_j_canoe_storm.push.success: You made it. The foreman paid you double for your nerve.
ev.amr_j_canoe_storm.push.failure: The boat capsized. You barely swam out and the load was lost.
ev.amr_j_tlacuilo.title: Rewriting history
ev.amr_j_tlacuilo.text: A noble lord asks you to repaint the genealogy in a book, adding a heroic ancestor who never existed. He offers as much as you earn in half a year.
ev.amr_j_tlacuilo.do.success: The heroic ancestor is now in place. The lord is pleased and will call on you again.
ev.amr_j_tlacuilo.do.failure: The temple's old books did not match yours. The forgery was discovered.
ev.amr_j_calpixqui.title: A tribute steward's post
ev.amr_j_calpixqui.text: A literate person is needed to keep the tribute books of a conquered town: how many cloaks, how much cacao and how many feathers it owes each term. The post is honourable and dangerous: the conquered hate tribute collectors.
ev.amr_j_chasqui_night.title: An urgent message
ev.amr_j_chasqui_night.text: At night a chasqui arrived from the next station with an urgent message for the governor. And your ankle is swollen from yesterday's run.
ev.amr_j_chasqui_night.run.success: You delivered the message in time. The governor remembered your name.
ev.amr_j_chasqui_night.run.failure: On the descent your leg gave way. You fell and could not get up for a long time.
ev.amr_j_chasqui_khipu.title: The khipu keeper's apprentice
ev.amr_j_chasqui_khipu.text: The khipu keeper at the relay station has noticed that you repeat messages word for word and never confuse the knots. He offers to take you as his apprentice.
ev.amr_j_khipu_audit.title: The cords do not match
ev.amr_j_khipu_audit.text: According to your khipu the storehouse should hold three hundred sacks of maize, but in fact there are just over two hundred. The curaca asks you to "retie" the knots before the inspector arrives.
ev.amr_j_khipu_audit.retie.success: The inspector counted cords, not sacks. The curaca is now in your debt.
ev.amr_j_khipu_audit.retie.failure: The inspector counted the sacks. You were punished along with the curaca.
ev.amr_j_khipu_chief.title: Head of the khipus
ev.amr_j_khipu_chief.text: The provincial governor is looking for a chief khipu keeper to bring together the whole census, all the storehouses and all the herds. You know the knots better than anyone.
ev.amr_j_rope_bridge.title: The grass bridge
ev.amr_j_rope_bridge.text: Every year the hanging bridge over the river is woven anew: thousands of grass cords, ropes as thick as a body. The most dangerous job is tying the new ropes over the gorge.
ev.amr_j_rope_bridge.climb.success: The bridge is strung. The old men say there has not been one so even in years.
ev.amr_j_rope_bridge.climb.failure: You slipped and hung from the safety rope. Your hands are torn raw, but you are alive.
ev.amr_j_cumbi.title: Cloth for the Inca
ev.amr_j_cumbi.text: The mamakuna have entrusted you with cumbi for the Inca himself: hundreds of threads to the palm and a pattern no one could mistake. He will wear it once and burn it.
ev.amr_j_cumbi.perfect.success: The mamakuna ran her hand over the cloth in silence and nodded. There is no higher praise.
ev.amr_j_cumbi.perfect.failure: A flaw in the pattern. All the work had to be unpicked.
ev.amr_j_cumbi.fast: Finish on time however it comes out
ev.amr_j_pachaka.title: A hundred without a captain
ev.amr_j_pachaka.text: Your captain fell during the siege of a northern fortress. The warriors of your hundred, all from neighbouring ayllus, are looking at you.
ev.amr_j_pachaka.lead.success: The fortress fell, and the Inca confirmed you as captain.
ev.amr_j_pachaka.lead.failure: The assault was beaten back. You were wounded and the hundred was given to another man.
ev.amr_j_ticitl.title: A noble patient
ev.amr_j_ticitl.text: You have been called to a noble lord: fever and cough, and the priests have already prayed. You know a strong remedy made from bark, but if he dies after taking it, you will be blamed.
ev.amr_j_ticitl.strong.success: Three days later the lord got up. You were richly rewarded.
ev.amr_j_ticitl.strong.failure: The lord grew worse. His family glares at you.
ev.amr_j_ticitl.text.cusco: You have been called to an Inca noble: fever and cough, and the coca diviners have already done their part. You know a strong remedy made from bark, but if he dies after taking it, you will be blamed.
ev.amr_j_ticitl.text.quito: You have been called to an Inca noble: fever and cough, and the coca diviners have already done their part. You know a strong remedy made from bark, but if he dies after taking it, you will be blamed.
ev.amr_f_nemontemi.title: The five empty days
ev.amr_f_nemontemi.text: The nemontemi have arrived, the five unlucky days at the end of the year. People stay indoors, do not wash, do not quarrel and start nothing new. And you have urgent work to do.
ev.amr_f_nemontemi.work.success: The work got done and nothing bad happened.
ev.amr_f_nemontemi.work.failure: The neighbours saw. Now every misfortune in the ward will be blamed on you.
ev.amr_f_blood_vow.title: A vow
ev.amr_f_blood_vow.text: When you were ill you promised the gods a gift: a few drops of your own blood, drawn from your ears with a maguey thorn, and a night's vigil at the temple. The illness passed. The gods are waiting.
ev.amr_f_blood_vow.gift: Bring gifts to the temple instead
ev.amr_f_cholula.title: Pilgrimage to Cholula
ev.amr_f_cholula.text: In Cholula, at the vast pyramid of the Feathered Serpent, the sick are said to be healed and vows fulfilled. Pilgrims come from every land. The journey takes several days.
ev.amr_f_mallki.title: The festival of the dead
ev.amr_f_mallki.text: In the month of the dead the ancestors are carried out of their tombs: dressed, offered chicha, carried round the fields and asked for advice. Your family is deciding how much to spend on grandfather.
ev.amr_f_pachacamac.title: The oracle of Pachacamac
ev.amr_f_pachacamac.text: On the coast stands the temple of Pachacamac, the most famous oracle in the Andes. Even the Inca sends questions there. If you bring gifts, the priests will pass your question to the god as well.
ev.amr_f_friars.title: The barefoot friars
ev.amr_f_friars.text: Friars in brown habits walk the ward, barefoot and thin. They take no tribute and teach children to sing in a foreign tongue. Their god, they say, wants no one's blood. Many neighbours have already been baptised.
ev.amr_f_friars.listen: Listen, but keep to your own gods
ev.amr_f_hidden_idols.title: Gods behind the altar
ev.amr_f_hidden_idols.text: You noticed that your neighbours have hidden a stone Tlaloc in the base of the new cross. A friar is searching for "idols" and promises a reward to anyone who points them out.
ev.amr_f_andes_priest.title: A cross over the huaca
ev.amr_f_andes_priest.text: A Spanish priest had the huaca stone by the spring smashed and set up a wooden cross in its place. Those who accept baptism are promised they will be left alone.
ev.amr_f_andes_priest.secret: Be baptised, but secretly bring offerings to the broken huaca
ev.amr_f_andes_priest.refuse: Go up into the mountains, away from the Spaniards
ev.amr_d_war_levy.title: The ward sends its warriors
ev.amr_d_war_levy.text: The ruler has declared a campaign. Every ward sends a company under its own banner. Your old teacher from the telpochcalli calls on you: "A captive is the road to honour for a commoner."
ev.amr_d_inca_levy.title: The Inca's army
ev.amr_d_inca_levy.text: The curaca has received orders: the ayllu must supply warriors for a campaign in the north. Sling and mace will come from the storehouses, and your family will be fed while you are away.
ev.amr_j_chasqui_pick.title: Legs for the royal road
ev.amr_j_chasqui_pick.text: The relay station on the royal road needs a new chasqui. The curaca has seen you running up the slopes after llamas and names you.
ev.amr_d_healer.title: The old healer
ev.amr_d_healer.text: The old healer at the edge of the ward says you have "hands that listen". She knows hundreds of herbs and will teach you if you carry her water and firewood.
ev.amr_d_healer.text.cusco: The old healer from the next ayllu says you have "hands that listen". She knows the herbs of the warm valleys and coca divination, and will teach you if you carry her water and brushwood.
ev.amr_d_healer.text.quito: The old healer from the next ayllu says you have "hands that listen". She knows the herbs of the warm valleys and coca divination, and will teach you if you carry her water and brushwood.
